title: Read a live process view
goal: Interpret a live process view without inventing a performance problem.
challenge: Locate owned processes in a live view, identify CPU/memory and niceness columns, explain load and available memory, and exit the tools cleanly. Zero CPU usage is a valid observation; no performance threshold is required.

steps.explanation: Create an identifiable sleeping task. No CPU stress is needed.
steps.expected: The task normally uses little or no CPU.
The display updates; NI is niceness and %CPU is sampled CPU activity, not a guaranteed value.

steps.command: Press q in the GTK guest console

steps.explanation: Compare a sorted snapshot with a live view.
steps.expected: ps %CPU uses a process-lifetime average; it need not match top's interval-based values.

steps.explanation: Repeat the snapshot every two seconds.
steps.expected: The header and output refresh. This does not change any process.

steps.command: Press Ctrl-C in the GTK guest console

steps.explanation: Read load averages and memory availability.
steps.expected: uptime shows 1/5/15-minute load averages. free shows available memory; cached memory is not automatically a fault.

steps.explanation: Clean up only the owned task you started.

hints: Use q to exit top; use Ctrl-C to exit watch.
A sleeping process is usually S and can have 0% CPU.
Load includes runnable tasks and tasks in uninterruptible wait; it is not a CPU percentage.
review: I located my process in a live view and understood the important columns.
I distinguished a snapshot, CPU activity, load and memory availability.
I exited the tools and cleaned up.
coverage: Real guest practice; completion is self-reviewed, with no guest assessment or verification score. Partial LPIC-1 103.5 coverage.
